Resolves #13018

The native Markdown renderer now preserves the first number of each ordered-list block. A producer's separated `1.` and `2.` recommendations previously rendered as two lists both starting at 1; the second now carries the standard `start="2"` attribute. This directly fixes rank display in the complete Golden Path reader, without rewriting its Markdown.

Evidence: L2 (the existing parser suite, including the new start-value regression) → L2 required for AC-1–3.

Micro-review eligible: contained — restores numbered-list semantics inside the existing parser; no new grammar or renderer.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Existing Parser spec covers separated rank 2 and explicit start 0, asserting native VDOM attributes. |
| AC-2 | The same regression checks default 1-based lists, unordered lists and their text; the previous list tests also pass. |
| AC-3 | All 22 parser tests pass, including stable IDs, streaming append and inert-content cases. |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive. The original streaming component remains unchanged outside list-marker preservation.

## Test Evidence
All parser coverage runs in the existing unit suite. The paired FM reader additionally checks the second rendered `ol` has `start="2"`; its installed proof remains in neomjs/neo-agent-institution#210.

## Post-Merge Validation
The paired reader pins the merged engine change and verifies the actual recommendation in installed FM.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** contained — it restores CommonMark ordered-list start semantics inside the existing parser. There is no new grammar, renderer or contract.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim: a separated `2.` block used to render as a second list starting at 1, and now carries `start="2"`, with `0` surviving too. I verified it against the exact head `aa313503`. `REGEX_OL_ITEM` gains a capture group for the number, so I checked every other reader of it. `:465` uses the match only as a boolean and `:593` uses `.test`, so the only group reader is the item loop (`:470–484`), which now takes the text from group 2 and the start from the first item only, as CommonMark specifies. There is a single list-VDOM builder (`:279`), and it emits `start` only when the block carries one. Default `1.` lists stay attribute-free (`startNumber !== 1`), so the prior shape and stable-ID behaviour are unchanged. The new arm pins rank 2, zero, a default list and an unordered list, and CI is 37/37 at this head. I looked for a second group-1 reader or a second list builder that would miss the start, and found neither. The repair touches no site outside the prescription.

**Findings:** None.
